heading: What Is Poor Mental Health Costing Your Business?
intro: Poor mental health costs UK employers around £51 billion a year — through sickness absence, people working while unwell, and staff leaving. Enter the size of your workforce to see an estimate for your organisation.
shareDescription: Poor mental health costs UK employers £51 billion a year. Find out what it could be costing your business in seconds.

sourceNote: This is an estimate based on UK averages, not a measurement of your organisation. The headcount estimate uses Deloitte's 2024 report "Mental health and employers", which puts the annual cost of poor mental health to UK employers at about £51bn: £23.8bn from presenteeism (working while unwell), £19.5bn from staff turnover and £7.3bn from sickness absence (rounded in the report's summary to £24bn, £20bn and £7bn). Dividing these by roughly 30 million UK employees to get a cost per employee is our own approximation. "Your figures" use the assumptions listed under "How we calculated this", which are ours, not Deloitte's.
ctaHeading: The good news: it can be reduced
ctaText: Deloitte's research found that, on average, employers got back around £4.70 for every £1 they spent on supporting their people's mental health. That is an average across many kinds of workplace mental health support, not a measured result of any particular training, including ours. Equipping managers to spot the signs early and support their teams is a practical place to start.
